items.q: In December 2025 total supermarket sales in Tykon rose by 10% to €12.05 billion compared with December 2024. Shop n Save's market share was 13.4% in December 2024 and 13.8% in December 2025. Calculate Shop n Save's revenue in December 2024.
items.why: December 2024 total = €12.05bn ÷ 1.10 = €10.95bn. Shop n Save = 13.4% × €10.95bn = €1.47bn. Taking 10% off €12.05bn gives the wrong base.
items.label: Paper 2 June 2026 Q01.1

items.q: A project costs £300,000 and lasts 4 years. Net cash flows are Year 1: £120,000; Year 2: £200,000; Year 3: £130,000; Year 4: £210,000. What is the average rate of return (ARR)?
items.why: Total net cash flow = £660,000. Total profit = £660,000 – £300,000 = £360,000. Average annual profit = £360,000 ÷ 4 = £90,000. ARR = £90,000 ÷ £300,000 × 100 = 30%. Taking off the cost of the investment is the step most often missed.

items.q: The decision tree shows two options. Which option should be chosen on financial grounds, and what is its net gain?
items.why: Option A: expected value = (0.4 × £27m) + (0.6 × £3m) = £12.6m. Net gain = £12.6m – £3m = £9.6m. Option B: expected value = (0.25 × £7m) + (0.75 × £2m) = £3.2m. Net gain = £3.2m – £2m = £1.2m. Option A has the higher net gain. Compare net gains, not expected values.

items.q: Purefields, 2025 (€m): revenue 68,187; gross profit 4,849; operating profit margin 4.14%. Calculate its operating expenses.
items.why: Operating profit = 4.14% × €68,187m = €2,823m. Operating expenses = gross profit – operating profit = €4,849m – €2,823m = €2,026m.
items.label: Paper 2 June 2026 Q01.2

items.q: A business has non-current liabilities of £150,000 and gearing of 50%. It takes out a new long-term loan of £100,000. What is its new gearing?
items.why: Capital employed before = £150,000 ÷ 50% = £300,000. The loan adds to both non-current liabilities and capital employed. New gearing = (£150,000 + £100,000) ÷ (£300,000 + £100,000) × 100 = 62.5%.
items.label: New question

items.q: A business has a 20% share of a market. The market grows by 25% and the business's sales stay the same. What is its new market share?
items.why: Take the market as 100 before the change. The business sells 20. The market becomes 125. New share = 20 ÷ 125 × 100 = 16%.
items.label: New question

items.q: A market was worth £240m in 2024 and £250m in 2025. What was the percentage change?
items.why: Percentage change = (new – old) ÷ old × 100 = (250 – 240) ÷ 240 × 100 = 4.2%. Divide by the old figure.
items.label: New question

items.q: Current assets £3m, Current liabilities £2.4m, Non-current liabilities £4.2m, Capital employed £12m. Gearing ratio?
items.why: Gearing = Non-current liabilities / Capital employed x 100 = 4.2/12 x 100 = 35%. Use the correct formula: NCL / Capital Employed x 100.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: A business has a gross profit margin of 25% on revenue of £25m. What is its cost of sales?
items.why: Gross profit = 25% × £25m = £6.25m. Cost of sales = revenue – gross profit = £25m – £6.25m = £18.75m.
